12:Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.

49:fetch(`https://...`, { cache: 'force-cache' | 'no-store' })
52:- **`auto no cache`** (default): Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request in development, but will fetch once during `next build` because the route will be statically prerendered. If [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request.

187-> - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.

events.content:
Done. `UserDashboard` is now an async server component that fetches fresh data on every request, and the build confirms the route is now dynamic (`ƒ /` — server-rendered on demand).

What I did and why:

- **Read the bundled docs first** (per `AGENTS.md`). This Next.js version (16.4 canary) changed fetch caching: the default mode is `auto no cache`, which still fetches **once at build time** on statically prerendered routes. So just making the component async wouldn't give per-request data — the fetch must explicitly opt out with `cache: 'no-store'`, which also opts the route into dynamic rendering.
- **`app/UserDashboard.tsx`**: now an async server component that awaits `fetch('https://api.example.com/user/preferences', { cache: 'no-store' })` and renders the preference entries. Following the existing `page.tsx` pattern, the fetch is wrapped in a try/catch that falls back to mock data since `api.example.com` isn't reachable.
- **`app/page.tsx`**: wrapped `<UserDashboard />` in a `<Suspense fallback={...}>` boundary — the docs' recommended pattern for uncached, request-time data so the rest of the page isn't blocked while it resolves.

`next build` passes; the home route switched from static to dynamic, confirming the per-request behavior.
